verdict.rationale: ClickUp lists "Automations" as a first-party product, and its developer docs say you can "Trigger workflows from ClickUp events", so it owns an automation capability. The evidence is only bare headings, with nothing describing building trigger-and-action rules. Integration-driven task creation (Calendly, Salesforce) and third-party n8n do not count toward the native capability. Missing for 10: documentation of the rule builder (triggers, conditions, actions), examples of eliminating repetitive steps, any limits or quotas, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can build trigger-and-action automation rules to eliminate repetitive manual steps
